l4_steps.name: Trigger wireless QAR data offload at gate
l4_steps.input: Aircraft weight-on-wheels signal; gate docking confirmation
l4_steps.output: Raw QAR binary file transferred to FOQA ground server
l4_steps.kpi: Offload completion within 10 min of gate arrival; flight coverage rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: WiFi connectivity gaps at remote apron stands force manual USB retrieval, adding 4–6 hr to processing queue and delaying same-day exceedance review

l4_steps.name: Validate data frame completeness and CRC integrity
l4_steps.input: Raw QAR binary file from Step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Validated flight data file or data gap report
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of flight duration; frame error rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Pre-2010 QAR units use proprietary frame formats requiring manual decoding — adds up to 2 hr per flight to the processing queue and delays exceedance detection

l4_steps.name: Ingest supplemental ACARS performance snapshots
l4_steps.input: Data gap notification from Step 1.2 or routine ACARS push
l4_steps.output: ACARS performance dataframes merged into consolidated flight record
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS data merge success rate ≥95%; gap-fill latency <30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS snapshot frequency (every 10–30 min) is too coarse to reconstruct fine-grained exceedance events; oceanic airspace has no ACARS coverage, leaving gap-fill as an estimate only

l4_steps.name: Execute automated exceedance detection run
l4_steps.input: Validated and merged flight data file from Phase 1
l4_steps.output: Exceedance event list with parameter name, recorded value, threshold, and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Detection run completion <30 min per flight; false positive rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold libraries require manual calibration per aircraft type variant (e.g., 737-800 vs MAX 8 have different structural limits); miscalibration generates false positives that erode crew confidence in the FOQA programme

l4_steps.name: Classify exceedances by severity Cat A/B/C
l4_steps.output: Classified exceedance report (Cat A = flight safety, Cat B = airworthiness, Cat C = crew technique)
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥97%; all Cat A events reviewed within 24 hr of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: IOSA audit and airline AQP programme use different category boundary definitions — maintaining dual threshold tables increases configuration error risk and complicates audit trail documentation

l4_steps.name: Escalate Cat A exceedance to Flight Safety
l4_steps.input: Cat A exceedance classification from Step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Safety investigation record opened; NOC and crew scheduling notified
l4_steps.kpi: Cat A notification delivered to Flight Safety Manager <2 hr of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: Integration between Safety Line FOQA and Intelex SMS is typically manual (CSV export/import), introducing notification latency that risks breaching 24-hour internal reporting SLAs and downstream regulatory filing windows

l4_steps.name: Extract engine performance parameters post-flight
l4_steps.input: Completed flight leg identifier; aircraft tail number
l4_steps.output: EGT margin, N1 deviation, fuel flow, vibration, and oil pressure time series per engine
l4_steps.kpi: Parameter extraction completeness ≥99.5%; processing latency <15 min post-landing
l4_steps.pain_point: GoDirect data feed latency for long-haul international operations can exceed 1 hr post-landing due to satellite link congestion, delaying trend detection for time-sensitive engine health events

l4_steps.name: Compare engine trends against MRO baseline
l4_steps.input: Engine parameter time series from Step 3.1; fleet engine health baseline in AMOS
l4_steps.output: Engine health trend report; deviation flags relative to fleet statistical baseline
l4_steps.kpi: EGT margin loss ≤1°C per flight cycle; alerts triggered at ±3σ deviation from fleet mean
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS engine baselines require manual update after each shop visit — stale baselines mask post-maintenance performance degradation and delay early warning detection of incipient failures

l4_steps.name: Raise maintenance alert for engine trend deviation
l4_steps.input: Deviation flag exceeding ±3σ threshold from Step 3.2
l4_steps.output: Corrective work order raised; borescope inspection scheduled against next available ground time
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance alert actioned within 4 hr of detection; on-wing unplanned engine removal rate <0.05 per 1,000 flight hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Tight aircraft utilisation (≥13 hr/day on narrowbody fleets) means borescope inspections are routinely deferred due to limited ground time, allowing early-stage engine degradation to progress to AOG events

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference event with ATC and meteorological records
l4_steps.input: Flagged exceedance event from Phase 2; flight leg metadata
l4_steps.output: Contextualised event report overlaying ATC radar track, METAR/SIGMET, and PIREP data
l4_steps.kpi: Contextualisation report completed within 48 hr of event detection
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC radar data access requires a formal request to the relevant ANSP in most regions, with turnaround of 3–10 business days — delays investigation timelines and risks crew debriefing weeks after the event

l4_steps.name: Conduct de-identified ASAP crew debrief
l4_steps.input: Contextualised event report from Step 4.1; crew roster for the flight
l4_steps.output: Crew disclosure statement; event narrative; de-identified ASAP safety report
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP debrief completed within 72 hr of event detection; crew voluntary disclosure rate ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew participation in ASAP is undermined in organisations with punitive safety cultures; legal protections for voluntary disclosures vary by jurisdiction, limiting debrief effectiveness for international crew members

l4_steps.name: Route finding to training or close investigation
l4_steps.input: Debrief outcome and root cause classification from Step 4.2
l4_steps.output: Training referral issued to LMS, or closed investigation record with corrective recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective action closure within 30 days; recurrence rate for same event type <5% within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated integration between Intelex SMS and airline LMS platforms — manual training referral process results in tracking gaps, unverifiable completion, and repeat exceedances from the same crew pairing

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly FOQA performance dashboard
l4_steps.input: Aggregated exceedance data and KPI metrics exported from Safety Line FOQA
l4_steps.output: FOQA monthly report; fleet-level performance dashboard published to safety portal
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by 5th calendar day of each month; ≥12 FOQA KPIs tracked and trended
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data export pipeline from Safety Line FOQA to Tableau breaks with each platform version upgrade — dashboard reconciliation consumes 3–4 hr/month of analyst time on non-value-adding data plumbing

l4_steps.name: Evaluate event against mandatory SDR reporting threshold
l4_steps.input: Completed investigation record; regulatory threshold matrix (FAR 121.703, IOSA ISM)
l4_steps.output: Regulatory reporting decision memo (SDR required Y/N; ASAP report required Y/N)
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory reporting decisions documented within 48 hr of investigation close
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.703 SDR thresholds are ambiguous for software-defined exceedances such as FMS autoflight anomalies — each case requires legal review, delaying time-sensitive filings and creating regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Submit SDR or ASAP report to FAA
l4_steps.input: Reporting decision memo and closed investigation record from Step 5.2
l4_steps.output: Filed SDR or ASAP report; FAA confirmation number recorded in SMS
l4_steps.kpi: SDR submitted within 96 hr of discovery per FAR 121.703; ASAP report submitted within 24 hr of event
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA DrAFT portal experiences 2–3 unplanned outages per year — no automated failover submission path means airlines risk missing mandatory filing deadlines and face potential enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Archive FDR and QAR data per FAR 91.609 retention policy
l4_steps.input: Validated FDR/QAR files, investigation records, and all associated reports
l4_steps.output: Archived data objects with retention metadata tags; automated deletion schedule per regulation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of FDR/QAR files archived within 24 hr of processing completion; retention period ≥25 hr (FDR per FAR 91.609), ≥2 yr (QAR programme data)
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS S3 lifecycle policy misconfiguration has caused premature deletion of QAR data at multiple carriers — audit trail gaps expose the airline to FAA enforcement action and inability to reconstruct accident sequences
